tweets.text:
"AI data centers are a cash drain. The chips get outdated and burn out."

No. That's an accounting fear dressed up as an economic one.

Every data center refreshes. CPU web servers run on 3-6 year cycles too. This is a faster clock, not a different business.

And outdated isn't worthless. A GPU cascades down a value curve. Training in years 1-2. Real-time inference in years 3-4. Batch and analytics in years 5-6. The proof is in the tape: $CRWV just booked 2020-era A100s into 2029, with prior-gen pricing at or above a year ago. Old silicon isn't getting dumped. It's re-leased at full freight.

And when you do refresh, you swap the cards, not the building. The power, cooling, and interconnect are the 6-8 year moat.

Here's the part the bears miss. Recurring capex isn't a cash drain. Sub-cost-of-capital returns are. Airlines buy planes forever. Telecoms rebuild networks forever. That doesn't make them drains. It makes them capital-intensive.

The real risk isn't the technology. It's whether that aging fleet stays leased and priced. Right now, the A100 says it does.

Such is the difference between reading a headline and reading a balance sheet.
